newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LIONS BRACED FOR SPRINGBOK CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS BRACED FOR SPRINGBOK CHALLENGE.

text.p: The British Lions have been warned to prepare for the most intense experience of their rugby lives when they embark next month on their first tour of South Africa for 17 years.

England lock Martin Johnson, named as captain of the 35-man squad announced on Wednesday, is under no illusions about what lies ahead on a 13-match tour including three tests and promised the Springboks a red-blooded confontation.
"The tests and provincial games are going to be more physical than any of the Five Nations games," acknowledged Johnson, one of six Leicester players named by the Lions selectors.

"I'm sure teams out there will physically intimidate us in a fair way and we've got to be ready to stand up to them. I don't think it'll be a dirty tour because international rugby has changed but it will be very physical."
The squad includes a number of players chosen for their physical assets, yet among 18 Englishmen there are surprise call-ups for flanker Neil Back and wing Tony Undewood.

Back has been ignored by successive England coaches for being too small and was banned for six months for manhandling the referee at the end of last season's English Cup final. He has now been reprieved to offer extra pace to the breakdown on the hard, fast South African grounds.

Speed has also won Underwood a late vote once it became clear that Irish winger Simon Geoghegan was not going to be fit enough to make the tour. England also provide wingers John Bentley and Nick Beal, who share just three caps between them.
Former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer's recommendation was enough to swing the captaincy for Johnson, who has never captained his country but is regarded as one of the best line-out performers in the world.

"He's got a very good dressing-room manner, and is totally respected by the players," said manager Fran Cotton. "We felt it was important to have someone in the heat of the battle in the forwards, someone whom the Springboks also had total respect for."

Ian McGeechan, on his third Lions tour as a coach, insists the squad contains enough options to give them a chance of emulating Willie John McBride's famous 1974 squad as the only British Isles side this century to win a test series in south Africa.

"What we've tried to do is have enough players on the field who are decision-makers," he said. "We're basically playing three World Cup finals in three weeks against the world champions on their own ground. We have to be tactically, physically and mentally ready to take them on.

"The early games of the tour will be very important. It will be very intense, we all appreciate that. I think South Africa are playing better than in their World Cup year. Tactically they're more fluid and they've got some new players."

A shortage of goalkickers has prompted the selectors to risk Welsh record point scorer Neil Jenkins, who broke an arm last month, and hire kicking guru Dave Alred to assist what is the first professional Lions party in rugby history.
England's Paul Grayson travels as cover, but there is no room for either South African-born Mike Catt or Jonathan Davies, who had both been heavily tipped in recent days.

Along with the English contingent, there are eight Welshman, five Scots and four Irishmen including prop Peter Clohessey, who has not played for his country since being banned for stamping on France's Olivier Roumat last year.
He will now tour with the Lions after being released from his contract with Queensland with whom he is currently involved in the Super 12 tournament.
